entries.title: Pennsylvania State Police guidance: skill game machines outside licensed premises are unlawful from October 14, 2026 and subject to criminal prosecution and immediate seizure
entries.facts: Pennsylvania State Police guidance states that on June 15, 2026 the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania ruled that skill games are "slot machines" as defined in the Gaming Act, and that under the Crimes Code slot machines are gambling devices which it is a criminal offense to own, operate or maintain without a license from the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board (PGCB). The guidance sets October 13, 2026 as the date by which "[b]usinesses and establishments must arrange to have skill game devices and related equipment removed," and states that from October 14, 2026 "[a]ll skill games devices/slot machines located outside of PGCB-licensed businesses are unlawful," with establishments that possess, operate or maintain them subject to criminal prosecution and immediate seizure. The listed consequences are seizure and forfeiture of the machines and associated equipment, seizure of proceeds from machine operation, criminal charges where deemed appropriate, and administrative citations against liquor licenses that may result in a fine, suspension or both. The guidance states that only licensed casinos and qualifying licensed truck stop establishments may possess and operate slot machines or video gaming terminals; that Section 5513 of the Crimes Code also reaches distributors, vendors and manufacturers that make, sell, lease or maintain slot machines without PGCB licensing and authorization; and that turning off, unplugging or temporarily disabling a machine does not change its status if it can still be readily operated.
entries.source_label: Pennsylvania State Police, Skill Games Resources (pa.gov), retrieved Oct. 14, 2026
entries.relevant_to: skill-game route operators, distributors and manufacturers, licensed casinos and truck-stop operators, bars and restaurants hosting terminals, and the payment providers serving them

entries.title: Interior publishes approval by operation of law of a Stillaguamish Tribe and Washington State class III gaming compact amendment effective October 14, 2026
entries.facts: At 91 FR 65252, published October 14, 2026, the Bureau of Indian Affairs announced the approval by operation of law of the Memorandum of Incorporation between the Stillaguamish Tribe of Indians and the Washington State Gambling Commission, an agreement the notice states governs "the operation and regulation of class III gaming activities." The notice states that "[t]he Compact revises Appendix E to increase the purchase price for a single scratch ticket and online wager limits to $50," and that "[t]he Compact takes effect on October 14, 2026." The notice does not refer to sports wagering.
entries.relevant_to: tribal gaming operators and their vendors, lottery-system suppliers, and state gaming regulators
